risks: We rely on a limited number of suppliers for raw materials and components.
We only carry key man insurance for our Chief Executive Officer.
We may incur substantial costs due to environmental regulations.
We may face securities class action litigation which could result in substantial costs and a diversion of management's attention and resources.
We face risks from potential future cybersecurity threats or incidents that could have a material adverse effect.

growth_drivers: Sidus Space has developed the Orlaith AI Ecosystem and Fortis™ VPX family of modular computing products.
Sidus Space validated imaging payload performance and advanced its Orlaith™ AI Ecosystem.
Our LizzieSat® platform is modular, flexible, and cost-effective, enabling rapid mission configuration and scalability.
Sidus Space is designing and building customized satellites for LEO and lunar applications for government and commercial entities.
Sidus Space offers hosted satellite and fleet services, leveraging patented technologies for cost-effective, vertical integration, and rapid delivery.
risks: The company may face lawsuits that could be costly and time-consuming.
Actual results may differ materially from forward-looking information.

growth_drivers: Investment in satellite platforms and AI-enabled computing technologies is intended to support future growth.
risks: The company may not achieve its financial projections and may need to raise additional capital.
The company faces risks from potential intellectual property infringement claims and lawsuits that could impact its business.

growth_drivers: Sidus Space is scaling satellite manufacturing and advancing commercialization of its Fortis VPX digital machine computing platform.
Sidus raised $159 million in gross proceeds in Q2 to strengthen its balance sheet and improve financial flexibility.
LizzieSat successfully completed vibration testing, a key milestone for its satellite program.
Fortis Maxima is Sidus' first flight for their FeatherEdge VPX Maxima digital mission computing platform.
Sidus Space anticipates initial full commercial availability of the Fortis BPX platform in early 2027.
risks: Revenue and gross margin declined, with costs of revenues decreasing more than revenues.
The company raised $146 million through two offerings, strengthening its liquidity position.
